paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita.) One baraita of his remains to us, cited several times in the Talmud, as in [Beitzah 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.13b.3) and [Menachot 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.54b.11): “It was taught: Abba Elazar ben Gimel says, ‘And your terumah shall be reckoned to you,’” etc. [Gittin 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.30b.13) reads ben Gamla, and [Bekhorot 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.58b.11) ben Gomel. The source of the baraita is [Sifrei Bamidbar 121, Korach](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Bamidbar.121.1), on “And it shall be reckoned,” and there it is Abba Elazar ben Gamliel (Gimel being an abbreviation of the name, in Hyman’s explanation), disagreeing there with Rabbi Yishmael.[^2]

notes.text: The consulted Beitzah 13b reads ben Gimel; Sifrei Bamidbar 121 reads ben Gamliel alongside Rabbi Yishmael. Hyman’s abbreviation explanation and statement that one baraita remains are not a new exhaustive attestation or identity finding.

The consulted Beitzah reads Gimel, Gittin Gamla, and both Menachot and Bekhorot Gomel. The Sifrei has Gamliel beside Rabbi Yishmael, as [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=560&lang=en) also records. Hyman explains Gimel as a short form.
